points.requirement: Preserve the cytokine/receptor, engineered trigger/growth and CAR-target/separate-support-receptor scenes, with schematic relays and no implication that cell accumulation proves safe tumour killing.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A synthetic cytokine receptor is an engineered cell-surface protein that connects a specified input to intracellular signalling. It differs from engineering a soluble cytokine or simply administering a cytokine. Some designs require an externally supplied ligand; others generate ligand-independent signalling. The receptor domains, input, expression and cell type define the tested construct. A growth-supporting signal does not itself establish antigen recognition, entry into a tumour, completed killing or durable patient benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional comparison with equal starting viable-cell input and the same CAR, a supplied trigger produces 250 viable cells at 48 hours versus 100 without it. That is 2.5 times the viable-cell count, not 2.5 times the treatment benefit. Tumour killing changes from 20 to 25 per cent, while a separate healthy-cell assay changes from two to 18 per cent injury. Count division, survival and loss separately, retain each assay’s target-cell denominator and uncertainty, and do not combine these results into a whole-body safety window.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Read each supportive feature as a testable hypothesis. A drug-triggered signal needs a baseline and a withdrawal test; an antigen-triggered signal needs testing after cells leave the priming site. Constitutive signalling raises different growth and cell-state questions, while a secreted payload can affect neighbouring cells or circulate. Orthogonal means sufficiently separate from natural partners under tested conditions, not selectivity established by its name. The supportive receptor does not specify the CAR target, and changing an internal signal is different from secreting a cytokine. An added support signal does not by itself demonstrate adequate oxygen, tissue access, recognition of an absent antigen or patient benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: JAK-STAT is a route used by many cytokine receptors rather than a synonym for every cytokine response. Engelowski’s artificial receptor/ligand systems tested defined signalling and growth responses. Stüber’s TGF-beta experiments measured a SMAD-associated response in ROR1 CAR T cells. Follow the specified receptor and measured pathway through to gene output and cell phenotype; a phosphate signal, feedback response, growth measurement and completed target killing are different observations.
evidence.explanation: Cytokines are receptor-dependent signalling proteins, not nutritional fuel; exposure and receiving-cell state shape the possible response. 29789554: primary research report, complete abstract and targeted whole passages only; not end-to-end full text; 32303620: primary research report, complete abstract and targeted whole passages only; not end-to-end full text

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Cytokines are signalling proteins whose binding to a suitable receptor changes signalling and gene expression in a receiving cell. Autocrine action is on the producing cell, paracrine action is on neighbours, and endocrine action is at a distance, for example after entry into the circulation. Distant action is possible rather than the default for every cytokine (British Society for Immunology, Cytokines: Introduction). Chemokines are a cytokine family involved in cell recruitment and can also affect leukocyte activation (NLM MeSH, Chemokines). The information-versus-fuel distinction is a reading rule: a measured amount of signalling protein does not measure the energy available to the cell, and a message without the relevant receptor and response machinery does not establish a response.
evidence.explanation: Cytokines are receptor-dependent signalling proteins, not nutritional fuel; exposure and receiving-cell state shape the possible response. points.requirement: Preserve separate tissue entry, target recognition, useful function and healthy-tissue safety barriers; improving one link or increasing cells does not establish the complete treatment chain.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A rise in engineered cells in blood with few found in two tumour biopsies leaves distribution and infiltration unresolved. Blood abundance is not entry into a mass of tissue, and a biopsy represents its sampled place and time. If a receptor works in a simple culture but killing falls in a more complex model with the target still present, investigate access, cell state and the model’s other features with controlled perturbations. The contrast alone does not identify a macrophage, vessel or signalling pathway as the cause, or show that more expansion will solve it. Expression of PD-1, LAG-3, TIM-3 or TIGIT, or a count of macrophages or suppressor cells, does not by itself establish which input caused the functional difference. Trafficking toward a site and infiltration into tissue are different steps, and vessel number does not measure perfusion. Chronic stimulation, low oxygen, limited nutrients and inhibitory signals are different hypotheses; exhaustion describes cell states rather than physical tiredness.
evidence.explanation: Entry, recognition, useful function and healthy-tissue harm are separate links; more cells do not establish a complete treatment chain. points.requirement: In the consensus vaccination assay, remove residual inducing chemical and add no separate adjuvant before vaccinating immunocompetent syngeneic mice with dying tumour cells. Assays consume tumour-cell aliquots, supernatant or host-model material and report separate dead-cell fractions, signal concentrations or surface staining and challenge incidence or growth. Fixed tissue cannot test later recovery, and no universal marker or arrest-duration cutoff works across contexts. Research outputs include method-defined cell fractions, marker intensities and longitudinal proliferation or regrowth. Stained sections and tested cells consume material. Formation, delivery and breakdown are separate steps; not all lysosomal processes use autophagosomes. points.requirement: More lipidated LC3-II can reflect greater formation or slower removal. points.requirement: Flux, selected-cargo clearance and survival dependence are different claims. NBR1 experiments identify selective ubiquitinated-cargo handling, not a universal LC3 cargo census. review.auditor: Coordinator integration; not expert sign-off
review.rationale: Both themes place illustrative oxidation in membrane tails and separate GPX4/glutathione lipid-hydroperoxide reduction from FSP1/CoQ radical-trap regeneration. Generic O icons are not atom counts or assay readings. The image explicitly requires damage, timing, death and rescue and disclaims diagnosis.

points.requirement: Ferroptosis involves iron-dependent membrane-lipid peroxidation causing death. Erastin experiments implicated cystine uptake through system xc-, connecting cysteine and glutathione supply to antioxidant defence. Vulnerable polyunsaturated lipid chains, iron availability and cellular conditions matter; general reactive-oxygen fluorescence does not establish this mechanism.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: GPX4 uses glutathione to reduce lipid hydroperoxides to lipid alcohols. FSP1 provides a parallel coenzyme-Q radical-trapping defence; it does not replace every GPX4 function or describe the whole protection network. Protein abundance alone does not measure protective activity or predict compound sensitivity.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: Assigning ferroptosis needs convergent measurements of death, lipid damage preceding death, iron dependence and appropriately controlled rescue. Independent genetic and chemical perturbations strengthen attribution; rescue alone is not complete proof. Probe chemistry, concentration, nutrients, cell density and observation time can alter results. A lipid-probe ratio and death fraction are different outputs, with no universal diagnostic staining threshold. Live death and rescue tests consume viable model material. Specify lipid-probe oxidation ratios and independently measured death percentages over a stated interval; a marker snapshot does not reconstruct the full causal sequence.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: A culture with abundant GPX4, a general oxidation signal and no death has not demonstrated ferroptosis. Cell-line and xenograft vulnerabilities do not establish tolerable exposure, selective cancer killing or benefit in patients. Alternative defences can confer resistance, so a strong antioxidant programme is not automatically a treatment vulnerability.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

review.rationale: Earlier reviewed teaching points are retained. Scientific interpretation is represented by the exact authored passages mapped in the batch packet. Artwork is not copied, and no equivalent reader-facing figure is claimed.

points.requirement: Ubiquitin is a small protein attached through enzyme steps: E1 uses ATP for activation, E2 carries activated ubiquitin, and E3 promotes substrate selection and transfer. Reticulocyte experiments separated these functions. E3 families differ in transfer mechanism; no single cartoon specifies all of them.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: Suitable tagged cargo can be unfolded by ATP-dependent proteasomal machinery and broken into fragments, while ubiquitin is removed and reused. Other ubiquitin signals organise interactions rather than destruction, and yeast experiments show overlapping chain functions. Lysosomal autophagy and proteasomal breakdown are distinct routes.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: Protein abundance reflects synthesis and removal. Measure named-substrate decay over time with synthesis, handling and viability controls; restoration of an E3 adaptor can strengthen attribution without proving direct binding or global proteasome failure. Catalytic activity per time, ubiquitinated-cargo intensity and protein lifetime in hours are different readouts. KEAP1 is one CUL3 adaptor for NRF2, so a CUL3 change cannot uniquely identify that substrate. Pulse labelling or a controlled temporary synthesis block can help estimate turnover but may cause stress. Independent perturbation and restoration help distinguish a selected-substrate effect from a secondary response; enzyme engagement alone does not establish selective killing.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: In a randomised trial of 669 people with relapsed myeloma after one to three prior therapies, bortezomib prolonged median time to progression compared with high-dose dexamethasone: 6.22 versus 3.49 months. This historical clinical result does not make an arbitrary E3 variant or abundant protein a predictive treatment biomarker.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

review.rationale: Both themes separate RNA processing through IRE1/XBP1u-to-XBP1s, PERK phosphorylation of eIF2alpha and ATF6 Golgi traffic/cleavage followed by a nuclear fragment. A phosphate alone does not specify kinase, total message is not splice fraction and branch activity is not death.

points.requirement: ER stress is an imbalance between protein-folding demand and local capacity; the unfolded protein response is an adaptation programme, not the same thing as the stress. IRE1 processes XBP1 RNA, PERK phosphorylates eIF2alpha and ATF6 processing releases a nuclear regulator. Distinct branches can alter folding capacity, incoming translation and disposal.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: ATF6 travels from ER to Golgi for processing; the released fragment, rather than the intact membrane-bound precursor, acts in the nucleus. Total XBP1 RNA differs from its splice-form fraction. Other kinases can phosphorylate eIF2alpha, so one phosphosite cannot identify the whole response.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: Specify preserved material, RNA quality, isoform-specific methods, total-protein controls, timing and identified cell populations. Splice-form fractions, processed ATF6 and defined phosphoprotein signals are different outputs. Increased XBP1 splicing with stable viable-cell counts supports a branch response, not lethal stress; measure growth and death directly and test causality independently. RNA or protein preparations and compatible tissue stains use material; functional dependence tests require viable cells. Report splice-form fractions, defined phosphosite signals or processed fragments with assay-specific controls, rather than a universal UPR-positive treatment threshold.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: XBP1 depletion altered tumour growth and relapse in defined triple-negative breast cancer models, with an HIF1alpha transcriptional interaction. Model findings and patient expression-signature associations do not establish universal XBP1 dependence, an assay cutoff or a treatment benefit. Successful stress adaptation can support survival.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

review.rationale: Both themes locate outer/inner membranes, intermembrane space and matrix; proton pumping is matrix-outward, ATP-synthase return and leak point inward, and electron transfer ends in oxygen-to-water separately. No fixed ratios are claimed. Source review of the foundational reconstitution claim remains open even though the actual image has been viewed.

points.requirement: Distinguish electron transport, proton pumping from the mitochondrial matrix to the intermembrane space, return through ATP synthase and leak. Treat the foundational reconstitution as a named artificial-vesicle coupling experiment, with its own orientation, rather than a universal cellular orientation or fixed proton-to-ATP ratio.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: Respiration and ATP generation are related but different measurements. Mitochondrial and nonmitochondrial oxygen consumption, proton leak and ATP-linked respiration require controlled separation. Respiratory transcripts, normalised oxygen-consumption rates and survival dependence cannot substitute for one another; bulk tissue composition and compensatory fuel use also matter. Oxygen-consumption assays require viable cells or functional preparations rather than routine fixed sections and use or perturb the tested material. Report oxygen per time with justified viable-cell or protein normalisation. Equal baseline respiration and different responses to ATP-synthase inhibition do not by themselves identify which culture will die.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: The fictional oxygen-rate example gives 60 minus 30 = 30 picomoles of oxygen per minute per 10,000 viable cells after ATP-synthase inhibition. This is an inhibitor-sensitive oxygen-rate difference, not picomoles of ATP, a death percentage or a corrected ATP-production calculation. Fuel, normalisation and assay controls remain attached.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: Extracellular acidification includes respiratory carbon dioxide as well as glycolytic acid production. Quantitative glycolytic or ATP-rate calculations need appropriate corrections and an identified method version; the contents of the published correction must be checked before adopting a corrected formula or conversion ratio.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

review.rationale: Both themes trace low-local-sterol SCAP/SREBP-2 movement from ER via vesicle to Golgi, a separate sufficient-sterol retention panel and cleavage releasing a fragment for nuclear entry. The whole precursor is not drawn entering the nucleus. No clinical sensing threshold follows from the schematic.

points.requirement: SCAP and local endoplasmic-reticulum sterol conditions regulate transport of membrane-bound SREBP to the Golgi. Processing releases a fragment that enters the nucleus and regulates lipid synthesis and uptake. Sufficient local sterol supply can retain the complex in the ER; total cellular cholesterol and SREBP RNA do not measure this processing.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: Identify the SREBP member and compartment: SREBP-2 is especially associated with cholesterol regulation, whereas SREBP-1 has major fatty-acid roles. Precursor, nuclear fragment, transcript, total sterol, uptake and synthesis rate are different readouts. A labelled production experiment answers a different question from an abundance snapshot.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: In the fictional supply experiment, nuclear SREBP-2 and uptake messages respond to lipid-poor medium; external lipid supply can reduce the response and compensate for synthesis perturbation. Record medium composition, density, timing and viability before assigning dependence. A supply-sensitive state does not establish the response of a person's tumour. Assess precursor and nuclear regulator, responsive transcripts, cellular sterols and uptake separately from labelled synthesis rates. Use controlled supplementation to test the proposed bottleneck; total amount does not specify production or local sensing.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: A statin inhibits HMG-CoA reductase in the mevalonate pathway, which supplies cholesterol and other products. Mevalonate rescue therefore cannot uniquely identify cholesterol as the limiting product. A pathway perturbation is not equivalent to every alteration of SCAP-SREBP regulation.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fibroblasts are cells; stroma is a broader compartment that also includes extracellular matrix, vascular structures and other cells. points.requirement: Alternative molecular regulation can alter HIF, so HIF protein or a hypoxia RNA signature is not a calibrated oxygen meter or proof of the same state in every region.

evidence.explanation: The exact reader paragraph carries this learning requirement at its stated model, sample, measurement or inference scope: Alternative molecular regulation can alter HIF, so HIF protein or a hypoxia RNA signature is not a calibrated oxygen meter or proof of the same state in every region.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: HIF-1 contains alpha and beta protein subunits. Under oxygen-replete conditions, oxygen-dependent modification of the alpha subunit enables VHL-associated degradation; limiting that regulation can stabilise it. Jaakkola and the Semenza review describe this mechanism and additional regulation. HIF RNA, alpha-protein stability and the resulting transcriptional response are different quantities. Alternative molecular regulation can alter HIF, so neither protein staining nor an RNA signature is a calibrated oxygen meter.

points.requirement: LoB concerns high-end blank/background response at a specified probability; blank noise, contamination and nonspecific signal require a distribution rather than one reading.

evidence.explanation: Semantic comparison at stated source or fictional-premise scope; hash and containment checks are separate from entailment.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The limit of blank describes an upper background response at a specified probability. A limit of detection concerns an amount that can be detected under stated false-call and detection-probability conditions; LoD95 specifies 95 per cent detection in the tested workflow. It is not a line above which every repeat must be positive, nor 95 per cent certainty that a person has disease. A limit of quantitation requires stated quantitative accuracy, including bias and imprecision goals. The limits answer different questions and have no universal spacing; they may coincide under a particular method and its criteria.

evidence.explanation: Semantic comparison at stated source or fictional-premise scope; hash and containment checks are separate from entailment.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: A prognostic marker is associated with a defined outcome under specified care in a defined population and time horizon. points.requirement: A vehicle control has the carrier without active treatment; untreated conditions can answer a different question if carrier has effects.

evidence.explanation: Semantic comparison at stated source or fictional-premise scope; hash and containment checks are separate from entailment.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. These are questions for matched model, timing and readout; no one control proves specificity or patient benefit, and agreement between similar readouts is not automatically independent mechanistic confirmation.

points.requirement: In the fictional100-to200 vehicle versus100-to100 drug comparison, endpoint count is50% of vehicle without measured net baseline decline; it is not50% killing. Death and recovery need separate measurements.

evidence.explanation: Semantic comparison at stated source or fictional-premise scope; hash and containment checks are separate from entailment.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional direct counts: vehicle-treated cells increase from 100 to 200 while drug-treated cells remain at 100. The endpoint drug count is half the vehicle count without measured net decline from the starting count, so calling it 50 per cent killing overstates the observation. Slower growth, death and a molecular change require their own readouts; direct death or recovery measurements could address further questions. Hafner and colleagues showed that conventional IC50 and maximal-effect measures depend on cell divisions during an assay and developed growth-rate metrics to address that dependence. A real experimental response does not by itself establish the responsible target or clinical benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional forest example: five studies compare treatment A minus control on the same 0 to 100 symptom scale at day 30. Their effects are -8, -6, -4, -2 and 0 points, each with standard error 2 and weight 20 per cent, so the square areas are equal. The mean is -4.0 points. With a classical moment variance estimate, Q = 10, I-squared = 60 per cent and tau-squared = 6 squared score points. A normal 95 per cent mean interval is about -6.8 to -1.2; the stated 2009 prediction method, using a t distribution with three degrees of freedom, gives about -13.0 to +5.0. The study intervals, mean diamond and wider prediction interval answer different questions. Five studies are few and these intervals are approximate; a negative mean does not imply a negative effect in every setting.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A confidence interval for the mean effect differs from a prediction interval for an underlying effect in another comparable study under the model. Neither is a personal prognosis interval. I-squared estimates the proportion of variability in study estimates associated with heterogeneity rather than sampling error; it is neither the percentage of people helped nor the percentage of studies that are wrong. Tau-squared is between-study effect variance on the chosen scale, such as squared score points or squared log risk ratios. These estimates can be uncertain, especially with few studies, and no I-squared cutoff alone makes pooling safe.

evidence.explanation: Semantic comparison at stated source or fictional-premise scope; hash and containment checks are separate from entailment.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional design: each of two donors supplies six wells, three control and three treated. A cancer-treatment history with surgery and continuing therapy cannot simply be reversed into an untreated comparison. These are interpretation examples, not instructions to change or interrupt care; clinical and research oversight remain separate.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fictional groups each contain 1,000 people, with complete reference assessment, no indeterminate results and assumed sensitivity 80 per cent and specificity 90 per cent. points.requirement: Carry the full labelled/unlabelled-binder visual: isotope, delivery, access, competition, clearance, retention, mass, activity and image time; the conceptual diagram supplies no uptake values.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Imagine sending a labelled binding tool into the body. Some remains in blood, some reaches accessible sites, and some fails to bind or clears. Delivery, access, target binding, competition, clearance and retention all affect the image. Therapeutic or unlabelled antibody can compete for the same target or alter distribution and background. A smaller signal after same-target treatment is therefore not, by itself, target loss. A conceptual labelled/unlabelled-binder drawing supplies these alternatives, not uptake values.

A prepared stained tissue section supplies a different, sampled observation.

points.requirement: Carry the whole echo-timing image: under common sound-speed assumptions later returns indicate deeper boundaries, while the selected plane supplies no histology or body census.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The room-echo analogy explains the observation: a beam travels into tissue and returns from boundaries. Under a common assumed sound speed, a later return is placed deeper than an earlier one. That relationship does not identify cell type. A selected image plane is neither a histological section nor a survey of the whole body. Grayscale images primarily describe echo patterns; Doppler uses frequency changes from movement to describe blood-flow direction or speed. Its displayed colours depend on the mode and settings, rather than staining malignant cells. Flow is not itself proof of malignant activity.

points.requirement: A shared beta chain can hide different alpha chains (figure, common confusions)

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: A shared beta chain can hide different alpha chains (figure, common confusions) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Beta match, alpha hidden, fictional: three cells carry beta chains B, B and C, so a bulk beta-chain view lists B, B, C and loses the alpha chains. The paired view keeps alpha X with beta B, alpha Y with beta B and alpha Z with beta C, so the shared beta B does not make alpha X and alpha Y equal. points.requirement: Density separation, interface, incomplete recovery and contamination; PBMC label is not purity (figure)

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Density separation, interface, incomplete recovery and contamination; PBMC label is not purity (figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: What the fraction is: peripheral blood mononuclear cells are circulating white blood cells with a single unsegmented nucleus, mainly lymphocytes and monocytes, with T, B and natural killer cells among them, isolated by layering anticoagulated blood over a density-separation medium and collecting the interface. Most conventional granulocytes and red cells separate elsewhere, but recovery is incomplete, so platelets, red cells or low-density granulocytes can contaminate a preparation, and the label PBMC does not guarantee purity. The classic density-gradient method dates from 1968 (Boyum 1968). Isolation selects a recoverable blood fraction and does not sample tumour or give a complete immune census.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Density separation, interface, incomplete recovery and contamination; PBMC label is not purity (figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The usable input for a downstream assay is the recovered viable cell preparation, not simply the volume of blood drawn. Fresh isolation, freezing, thawing, washing and any rest period define a sequence of selections, so record recovery, population composition and purity as well as viability. The Cytiva density-separation handbook describes the mononuclear interface, platelet carryover and possible immature-granulocyte contamination in pathological blood. That manufacturer method source does not validate every cancer assay, and an inadequate number of the relevant cells can make a rare-response experiment uninformative.

points.requirement: Multivalent avidity on a labelled scaffold (figure); tetramer as one format

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Multivalent avidity on a labelled scaffold (figure); tetramer as one format Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: What the evidence shows: in the original report, tetramers of HLA-A2 with two HIV-derived peptides or an influenza A matrix peptide bound peptide-specific cytotoxic T cells in vitro and T cells from the blood of HIV-infected people, and binding in general correlated well with cytotoxicity assays (Altman 1996). That is a correlation in those systems and not a rule that binding equals killing for an arbitrary tumour peptide. Tetramers are made by mixing biotinylated MHC with fluorescent streptavidin, and a later method made them with small-molecule fluorophores (Ramachandiran 2007), so reagent preparation is a source of variation. An observed stain shows binding under the tested conditions and does not show natural processing and display of that pair by a tumour.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Multivalent avidity on a labelled scaffold (figure); tetramer as one format Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Avidity describes the combined strength of multiple contacts. Multimerising peptide-HLA ligands can make binding detectable when an individual receptor-ligand contact is weak; the 2021 guidelines also caution that more multimerisation does not always improve detection. The measured output is a gate-defined binding fraction or, with a suitable counting method, a count. Reagent, viability and background controls support that binding measurement, which still requires separate validation before use for treatment selection.

points.requirement: Stimulus types, transport inhibition window, fixation and permeabilisation, viability stain before fixation (Mermaid, figure)

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Stimulus types, transport inhibition window, fixation and permeabilisation, viability stain before fixation (Mermaid, figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Method card, what it measures: cytokines retained inside cells during a defined assay, so a response can be assigned to stained cell populations. How: cells get a defined stimulus, a protein-transport inhibitor is present for a stated window so newly made cytokines accumulate, the cells are fixed and made permeable, and flow cytometry reads cytokine stains beside population markers, with a viability stain applied before fixation. Input: viable blood or tissue cells, with separate aliquots per stimulus, and fixed cells cannot go on to living-cell assays. Output: percent cytokine-positive cells within a named parent population, or percent with stated cytokine combinations. Controls: unstimulated or vehicle, a positive stimulation, viability and recovery, single-stain and staining-boundary controls. It cannot tell natural tumour presentation, direct target-cell killing, receptor sequence identity or clinical benefit.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Stimulus types, transport inhibition window, fixation and permeabilisation, viability stain before fixation (Mermaid, figure) Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The stimulus changes the question. Added peptide can bypass some processing steps; whole protein needs suitable antigen-presenting cells and processing, while broad stimulation tests responsiveness without identifying the intended antigen. The 2021 flow-cytometry guidelines describe brefeldin A and monensin as transport inhibitors and explain that their choice and exposure window can affect what is measured. Intracellular accumulation after inhibition is not a measurement of how much cytokine reached the surrounding medium.

points.requirement: Relative enrichment versus absolute expansion: 30 of 100 to 30 of 50 (figure); richness is not evenness; a shared sequence is not proven cancer specificity; one number is not the whole repertoire

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Relative enrichment versus absolute expansion: 30 of 100 to 30 of 50 (figure); richness is not evenness; a shared sequence is not proven cancer specificity; one number is not the whole repertoire Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Share against count, fictional: clonotype A is 30 of 100 measured molecules, 30%, and later 30 of 50, 60%. Its measured count did not rise, the total fell, and its relative frequency doubled, so relative enrichment is not absolute expansion and the molecule counts are not blood cell counts. In a published analysis pipeline, clonality was identified as a robust key metric and first choice for measuring TCR repertoire diversity, and in prostate cancer patients given sipuleucel-T the pipeline detected changes in sequence frequency and diversity in blood and prostate tissue (Zhang 2017); that is a methods and example study and sets no response threshold. A diversity-analysis software suite reports repertoire comparison and diversity outputs (Shugay 2015), and formulas, software settings and subsampling depth have to be stated.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Relative enrichment versus absolute expansion: 30 of 100 to 30 of 50 (figure); richness is not evenness; a shared sequence is not proven cancer specificity; one number is not the whole repertoire Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Frequency arithmetic, fictional: clonotype A is 10 of 10,000 sampled receptor units at baseline (0.1%) and 20 of 1,000 later (2%). The measured relative frequency rose twentyfold, but these are sampled receptor units and not a census of cells, and other populations contracting, different sampling and method effects can change frequency. Read counts are not always cell counts, because preparation, amplification and transcript abundance can change them, and absolute expansion needs compatible cell-number evidence. A sequence overlap between blood and tumour is detected overlap under a clonotype definition and is not a target, and antigen specificity needs a matching controlled recognition experiment.

points.requirement: Compare four equal versus four uneven clonotypes and a separate two-equal-clonotype sample to distinguish richness from evenness; the counts are fictional measured molecules, not body-wide cells.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Compare four equal versus four uneven clonotypes and a separate two-equal-clonotype sample to distinguish richness from evenness; the counts are fictional measured molecules, not body-wide cells. Exact current passage is retained in the batch proof packet; this field evidence is draft-local, not main or expert acceptance.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Metrics and arithmetic, fictional: with natural logarithms Shannon entropy is H = minus the sum of p times ln p, and one normalised clonality convention is 1 minus H / ln K for K observed clonotypes greater than one. Four clonotypes at 25, 25, 25 and 25 of 100 measured molecules give H = ln 4 = 1.386 and clonality 0. The same four at 70, 10, 10 and 10 give H = 0.940, clonality 1 minus 0.940 / 1.386 = 0.32, and an effective number of clonotypes exp(H) = 2.56. Richness is four in both, so many identities can coexist with strong dominance. Software may report Shannon entropy, its exponential or a normalised score, and these are not interchangeable: in the VDJtools documentation the Shannon-Wiener index returns the exponent of the entropy and the normalised index returns the entropy divided by the log of the clonotype count, which is evenness and not 1 minus that ratio, so a clonality built as 1 minus normalised entropy is a different number from either.

evidence.explanation: Coordinator semantic comparison: Compare four equal versus four uneven clonotypes and a separate two-equal-clonotype sample to distinguish richness from evenness; the counts are fictional measured molecules, not body-wide cells. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Effective-diversity measures weight a distribution differently. For the inverse-Simpson convention, define D as the sum of squared clonotype fractions and report 1 / D: four equal fractions of 0.25 give 4, whereas 0.70, 0.10, 0.10 and 0.10 give 1 / 0.52, about 1.92. This differs from the Shannon effective diversity of about 2.56 for the same uneven distribution. A fictional sample containing only A and B at 50 molecules each has richness 2 and equal weights; low richness does not imply unequal weights.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A count is a recovery under rules: enrichment concentrates candidate cells before identification, and each method selects. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Measure, then infer: the measured features are fragment length, end sequences, genomic positions and chemical marks. A reference or trained model then turns them into a source estimate or a score, so the output is an inference and not a cell census, and no single fragment carries a cancer address. Tumour fragments are shorter on average, but most short fragments in a sample still come from normal cells because normal DNA outnumbers tumour DNA when the tumour fraction is low. These features can complement mutation tracking when few informative mutations are sampled, and neither a source estimate nor a score by itself establishes tumour location, stage, a resistance mechanism or benefit from acting on a result.

Validation has to follow the measured feature: retain collection and processing dates, reference mixtures and process controls, batch checks, and the population, assay version and cut-off used to develop and evaluate the model. A satisfactory DNA yield or size distribution does not validate fragment-end patterns. Analytical reproducibility of a feature is separate from cancer detection, prognosis and benefit from acting on the score.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Measure, then infer: the measured features are fragment length, end sequences, genomic positions and chemical marks. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Design contract, from the FDA guidance of November 2024: a tumour-informed approach sequences the tumour and selects variants to follow. Its stated advantage is potentially higher specificity, and its limits include lag between tumour testing and panel creation, possible failure to detect mutations that emerge after tumour sampling or revert, and dependence on the number and reliability of selected targets, which may be better for tumours with higher mutation burden and well-characterised hotspot variants. A tumour-naive or tumour-agnostic panel is generic, with faster turnaround as its stated advantage and tumour biomarkers outside the panel as a limit. Both still meet the same finite plasma tube, background attribution and calling rules.

points.requirement: Fixed, snap-frozen and viable preparations preserve different properties. Recovered molecules do not establish living-cell function, and every preparation needs suitability checks for its intended assay.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded material preserves architecture and supports assays validated for its altered molecules, but cannot restore the original living cells. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Masuda experimentally demonstrated chemical modifications of fixed RNA and effects on amplification. evidence.supportingExcerpt: RNA quality assessment uses an aliquot of an extract, which itself consumed specimen material. points.requirement: Four panels: purified binding, engagement in relevant cell, effect measurement, benefit and harm evidence; reaching the compartment alone is insufficient; molecular shapes schematic.

evidence.explanation: Purified binding, relevant-system engagement, functional effects and clinical outcomes form separate evidence layers.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Target engagement and the evidence ladder. Target engagement asks whether a compound interacts with its intended target in the relevant system. Binding to a purified protein does not show that the compound enters the cell or reaches its target in a tumour, and engagement is also not a change in the target's function, a downstream effect or clinical benefit. Each question needs its own measurement: engagement first, then a measured biological effect, then a check of the causal explanation with controls, then clinical evidence.

evidence.explanation: Purified binding, relevant-system engagement, functional effects and clinical outcomes form separate evidence layers.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading a thermal-shift result. The cellular thermal shift assay was introduced to evaluate drug binding to target proteins in cells and tissue samples through ligand-induced thermal stabilisation (Martinez Molina et al. 2013). The readout is the soluble target signal remaining after heating, plotted either against temperature at a fixed compound concentration or against concentration at a fixed temperature, so degrees Celsius and concentration units sit on different axes and the two designs ask different bounded questions. A shift of the compound curve against a matched control supports engagement under those conditions; indirect stability or protein-complex effects can also change the signal, so it is not an inhibition or occupancy percentage, and no universal shift cut-off is given here. The heated aliquots are consumed, so a record should carry the compound, concentration, exposure time, temperature series, cell or tissue system and controls. In an isothermal-shift study with a pan-kinase inhibitor, a large share of non-kinase proteins shifted in cells, which the authors read as in-cell profiling being more likely than lysate profiling to identify indirect binding targets; they recommend lysate profiling to identify targets and in-cell profiling to verify intracellular engagement (Ball et al. 2020).

evidence.explanation: Purified binding, relevant-system engagement, functional effects and clinical outcomes form separate evidence layers.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: The last step is clinical. Mechanistic plausibility does not show benefit, because the target may also be present in healthy tissue and the useful margin depends on achieved benefit and harm in a stated disease, treatment setting, product and outcome. The National Cancer Institute adds that cancer cells can become resistant to targeted therapy when the target itself changes so the drug can no longer interact with it, or when cells find new ways to grow that do not depend on the target.

points.requirement: Read both complete receiver/exposure figures: the same cytokine can meet different receptors and states, and a local origin can yield distant exposure if signal reaches circulation and persists.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Circulating protein, local formulations and engineered cytokine-producing cells are different exposure strategies. A local origin does not guarantee local confinement: the signal can reach the circulation and persist elsewhere. In Zhang's 2015 dose-escalation study, 33 people with metastatic melanoma received transferred tumour-infiltrating cells engineered with inducible IL-12. Higher cell doses were associated with high serum IL-12 and interferon gamma and serious liver, fever and circulatory toxicities. The finding concerns that construct and regimen; it does not establish the safety or harm of every armoured cell product.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A cytokine is a signalling protein, and cytokine treatment supplies the protein or causes cells to produce it. The response depends on the molecule, the receiving receptor system, the cell's previous state and its exposure. A neighbourhood-message analogy is useful only to this extent: receiving a signal does not give a cell the correct cancer target or a literal instruction to fight it. IL-2 can influence lymphocyte growth and activity; interferons have different receptors and effects, so one cytokine name cannot stand for every immune signal.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: PI3K, AKT and mTOR name different parts of a signalling network. A diagram showing this route leaves other branches out.

points.requirement: CAR T/target/macrophage signalling; vessel cutaway with dashed arrows to blood-pressure and oxygenation; clinical attribution and named ASTCT version supply grade, cytokine concentration does not; no management algorithm.

evidence.explanation: Multicellular inflammatory signalling is interpreted through clinical attribution, competing causes, treated denominator and product-specific observation, not a cytokine curve.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Cytokine release syndrome can follow activation by engineered immune cells or T-cell-engaging treatments. Signals from several cell types can contribute to fever, hypotension, hypoxia and other organ effects. Infection or other conditions can produce similar findings or coexist with the syndrome.

evidence.explanation: Multicellular inflammatory signalling is interpreted through clinical attribution, competing causes, treated denominator and product-specific observation, not a cytokine curve.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading CRS without over-reading a cytokine level. CRS is a clinical syndrome, graded from attributed findings and not from a cytokine concentration. In a mouse model of CD19 CAR T-cell CRS, severity was mediated not by CAR T-cell-derived cytokines but by IL-6, IL-1 and nitric oxide from the recipient's macrophages, and IL-1 blockade abated it (Giavridis et al.); that supports a multicell amplification mechanism and does not show the same sources or shares in every human product. Infection and other conditions can cause or accompany the same findings, so the cause of a fever cannot be read from timing alone. A comparable report gives its grading version, observation window and treated denominator, with onset, maximum grade, interventions and resolution. Safety belongs to the product, disease, tumour burden and preparation, so experience with one blood-cancer product does not supply a solid-tumour product's rate, and no severe CRS in a small early study does not rule out uncommon events. CRS is a different problem from injury to healthy tissue that carries the target (on-target, off-tumour) and from neurotoxicity (ICANS). The treatment need not carry a cytokine payload to trigger endogenous inflammatory signalling. Tumour response does not establish acceptable inflammatory risk, and mild CRS does not establish lack of anticancer activity. Stopping a treatment input does not guarantee immediate removal of released signals or established injury. In a fictional early study, no severe CRS and a modest cytokine rise would not make every fever harmless CRS: attribution, clinical findings, a named grading framework, treated denominator and observation window are still needed.

points.requirement: Three panels: gut-brain nerve signalling plus blood-borne and learned inputs; reporting windows 0-24 h and beyond 24 h with overlap; nausea and vomiting as separate outcomes; no vomiting does not establish no nausea.

evidence.explanation: Separate gut/brain and learned pathways support overlapping timing categories; nausea and vomiting remain distinct outcomes.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Nausea and vomiting are different outcomes. Nausea is the sensation and vomiting the expulsion; they often occur together but one can occur without the other. Serotonin acting at 5-HT3 receptors and substance P acting at NK1 receptors contribute with other transmitters, and in two phase II cisplatin studies serotonin appeared to dominate early vomiting and substance P the later phase, with overlap (Hesketh et al.), so acute and delayed are reporting windows and not sealed pathways. The NCI PDQ classes are acute (the first 24 hours after chemotherapy), delayed, anticipatory, breakthrough, refractory and chronic; anticipatory nausea was reported in about 29 per cent of patients and anticipatory vomiting in 11 per cent, with prevalence varying with definitions and methods. It lists other causes too, such as fluid and electrolyte imbalance including hypercalcaemia or volume depletion, and tells clinicians to consider all potential causes when people receive several treatments, so new nausea needs a cause assessment.

evidence.explanation: Separate gut/brain and learned pathways support overlapping timing categories; nausea and vomiting remain distinct outcomes.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Gut-to-brain nerve signalling, blood-borne inputs and learned associations can contribute, so one blocked route does not account for every symptom. The timing terms organise observations. Acute commonly refers to the first 24 hours, delayed to symptoms beyond 24 hours, anticipatory to symptoms before treatment associated with previous experiences, and breakthrough to symptoms despite prevention. Learned symptoms are real; delayed does not mean mild, and early and later responses can overlap with multiday treatment. Prevention and treatment of symptoms that have appeared are different questions. In a fictional trial, no vomiting and no rescue medicine can meet its complete-response endpoint while the participant still reports nausea. Relief of either symptom does not measure tumour response.

points.requirement: Sam: no vomiting, persistent nausea, met endpoint no vomiting/no rescue -> not "no symptoms"; report separately, check window; emetic-risk class != individual certainty.

evidence.explanation: The named Navari regimen and endpoint definitions show why no vomiting/no rescue does not mean no nausea; patient reporting and alternative causes remain visible.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading antiemetic trials. In Navari et al. (380 evaluable chemotherapy-naive adults given cisplatin at 70 mg per square metre or more, or cyclophosphamide-doxorubicin, all with dexamethasone, an NK1 antagonist and a 5-HT3 antagonist), nausea prevention was the primary endpoint and complete response (no emesis and no rescue medication) a secondary one. No nausea in the first 24 hours was 74 per cent with olanzapine against 45 per cent with placebo, while complete response was 86 per cent against 65 per cent, so a complete response does not mean no nausea, and a person with no vomiting can still have persistent nausea. MASCC and ESMO updated their regimen-specific guideline in 2023 (Herrstedt et al., published 2024). Read patient-reported nausea severity, vomiting episodes, rescue-medication use and the observation window together with the preventive regimen and adherence; symptoms that limit drinking or eating warrant prompt contact with the care team. This describes how to read endpoints, not a medicine schedule.

points.requirement: Blood-side signals vs vascular lining/brain side with dashed arrow; ICE and broader domains feed clinical assessment; separate fictional CRS and neurologic timelines with no typical order/duration.

evidence.explanation: Neurologic findings and their timing are assessed separately from CRS, with vascular associations scoped to the Gust cohort and competing causes retained.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, or ICANS, is a neurologic syndrome associated with immune-effector-cell therapy. Changes in language, attention, handwriting or awareness and more severe findings such as seizures need assessment against baseline and alternative explanations. An immune-marker plot does not establish the syndrome.

evidence.explanation: Neurologic findings and their timing are assessed separately from CRS, with vascular associations scoped to the Gust cohort and competing causes retained.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: What is known about mechanism, timing and attribution. In 133 adults given CD19 CAR T cells, Gust et al. found that those with severe neurotoxicity had endothelial activation (disseminated intravascular coagulation, capillary leak) and increased blood-brain barrier permeability, and that the permeable barrier failed to protect the cerebrospinal fluid from high systemic cytokine concentrations including interferon-gamma. Higher risk went with acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, high marrow CD19-positive burden, high CAR T-cell dose, CRS and pre-existing neurological disease, and markers of endothelial activation before lymphodepletion were higher in people who later had grade 4 or worse neurotoxicity. That is an association in one product class and population, not a complete mechanism for every treatment. ICANS can accompany CRS or follow its own timetable, and neurotoxicity after CRS is scored separately, so recovery of blood pressure and oxygen does not show neurological recovery. If a person is confused while taking a sedating medicine and the ICE score falls, the grading rule requires that sedation be excluded, so the fall calls for clinical assessment, neither ignored nor diagnosed from the score alone. Clinical assessment also considers infection, metabolic disturbances, medicines and pre-existing neurologic disease. A safety report should retain onset, severity, attributed cause, interventions, duration, recovery and how many people were adequately observed. Separate fictional CRS and neurologic timelines can end at different times; they do not specify a typical order or duration. Stopping an engineered input does not guarantee immediate reversal of established neurologic injury.

points.requirement: Three locations (no depicted effect, gene interruption, regulatory insertion) then fictional clone descendants without assuming cancer; nonviral systems can integrate.

evidence.explanation: Site, vector-copy, expression and pathology measurements have sampling limits; the fictional expanding clone does not itself establish cancer.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: To attribute a malignancy after engineered-cell therapy, investigators ask whether the therapeutic sequence is present in the malignant cells, where the integrations are, whether they alter relevant genes, whether related clones were detectable earlier, and what prior therapy, underlying disease and pre-existing genetic changes contribute. Integration-site sequencing maps insertion locations, quantitative DNA assays estimate vector copies per cell, and flow cytometry, gene-expression measurement and pathology answer different questions about identity, function and malignancy; the sample is consumed by testing. Average vector copy number cannot show the position or effect of each insertion, a clone's frequency depends on the sampled cells, assay sensitivity and time, and blood may not represent every tissue. This record gives no copy-number or clone-frequency threshold because none of the sources read sets one. Messenger RNA delivery that does not integrate does not use genomic insertion as its route, which does not remove its other risks.

evidence.explanation: Site, vector-copy, expression and pathology measurements have sampling limits; the fictional expanding clone does not itself establish cancer.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional follow-up example, an engineered-cell clone becomes more common but no new malignancy has been established. The observation prompts examination of the clone, insertion sites, gene effects and clinical findings. A growth pattern, a malignant diagnosis and an insertion-driven mechanism are separate claims. An insertion that leaves no demonstrated gene effect, one that interrupts a gene and one that alters nearby regulation are different possibilities; none of those schematic locations assigns an incidence or time to cancer. A CAR-positive malignancy can establish product ancestry without identifying which change drove it.

evidence.explanation: Site, vector-copy, expression and pathology measurements have sampling limits; the fictional expanding clone does not itself establish cancer.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Some gene delivery systems, including the viral vectors used to make engineered T cells and to correct inherited immune disorders in blood stem cells, insert a genetic cassette into the cell's genome. Integration is the event; insertional mutagenesis is a consequential change that the event causes, such as interrupting a gene or altering the activity of a nearby one. Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

Integration alone does not establish a harmful biological consequence. A cell that gains a growth advantage passes the insertion to its descendants and a clone expands, but a growing clone is not a diagnosis of cancer, because a useful therapeutic response can also expand a clone. FDA's long-term follow-up guidance for gene therapy (January 2020) explains why the question is taken seriously: the biological activity of retroviral vectors and transposon elements is imparted by an integration event, such integration is in general not directed to specific sites, and that raises the potential for disruption of critical host genes or activation of proto-oncogenes near the site, and so the risk of malignancy. A nonviral transposon is therefore also an integrating system, and genome editing can produce its own undesirable changes with a risk of malignancy, which is a separate mechanism from vector insertion.

points.requirement: Clone becoming more common without malignancy does not prove insertional cancer; growth pattern, diagnosis, mechanism are separate claims.

evidence.explanation: Site, vector-copy, expression and pathology measurements have sampling limits; the fictional expanding clone does not itself establish cancer.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: To attribute a malignancy after engineered-cell therapy, investigators ask whether the therapeutic sequence is present in the malignant cells, where the integrations are, whether they alter relevant genes, whether related clones were detectable earlier, and what prior therapy, underlying disease and pre-existing genetic changes contribute. Integration-site sequencing maps insertion locations, quantitative DNA assays estimate vector copies per cell, and flow cytometry, gene-expression measurement and pathology answer different questions about identity, function and malignancy; the sample is consumed by testing. Average vector copy number cannot show the position or effect of each insertion, a clone's frequency depends on the sampled cells, assay sensitivity and time, and blood may not represent every tissue. This record gives no copy-number or clone-frequency threshold because none of the sources read sets one. Messenger RNA delivery that does not integrate does not use genomic insertion as its route, which does not remove its other risks.

points.requirement: 2000 WBC/uL x 20% = 400; 500 x 40% = 200 lymphocytes/uL: fraction doubles, count halves; no tumour kill measurement.

evidence.explanation: Serial absolute counts, fraction denominators, protocol context and harms are separate from cell-product or tumour-response outcomes; 400 versus 200 cells illustrates the distinction.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Counts need their denominators. A percentage of white cells is not an absolute count: with invented numbers, 20 per cent of 2,000 white cells per microlitre is 400 lymphocytes, and a later 40 per cent of 500 is 200, so the fraction doubled while the count halved. Lymphocyte and neutrophil counts are separate measurements, cytopenia means a low count of any blood cell type, and none of these measures tumour killing.

evidence.explanation: Serial absolute counts, fraction denominators, protocol context and harms are separate from cell-product or tumour-response outcomes; 400 versus 200 cells illustrates the distinction.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Lymphocytes include T cells, B cells and natural killer cells. Preparation can affect competition, regulation and, for donor products, host rejection; it can also act on cancer directly. It does not create a missing tumour antigen or guarantee that transferred cells enter a solid tumour. The need for preparation and its recovery criteria belong to the named protocol, rather than to every cell therapy. Serial blood counts consume blood samples rather than tumour tissue. Report absolute lymphocytes and neutrophils with units, sampling time and reference ranges, and measure transferred-cell number, location and function separately from the counts. More depletion is not automatically more benefit. Nonmyeloablative describes a regimen not intended to eliminate marrow blood production completely, rather than a promise of mild count suppression. Report severity, duration, recovery, infections, organ harms and relevant support with the regimen. More transferred cells, more depletion and more tumour killing are separate propositions.

points.requirement: Two fictional ANC curves share day 3 = 0.5 x10^9/L; A brief dip, B days 2-4 at 0.5; no infection probability or G-CSF threshold; same number does not establish same risk.

evidence.explanation: ANC units, depth, duration, timing and fever definition are retained; equal day-three values do not give equal course or infection probability.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading a neutrophil count. The absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is the number of neutrophils per volume of blood, written as cells per microlitre or as times 10 to the ninth per litre; it is more specific than the total white cell count, which includes other cell types. One ANC is a snapshot. Two invented curves make the point: both read 0.5 times 10 to the ninth per litre on day 3, but in one the count dips briefly and recovers, while in the other it stays at that level from day 2 to day 4. The matching number does not mean matching risk, because depth, duration and trend matter, and a count alone neither establishes nor excludes infection. Keep the sampling date, units, the laboratory's reference range and the place in the treatment cycle with the number. NCI patient guidance lists a temperature of 38 degrees Celsius or higher among the signs of infection to report promptly, whatever an earlier count showed. Better counts and fewer infections are related but separate outcomes, and neither is tumour response.

evidence.explanation: ANC units, depth, duration, timing and fever definition are retained; equal day-three values do not give equal course or infection probability.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: For a prevention study, retain the actual anticancer regimen, risk factors, comparator, fever-and-count definition and observation window. A toxicity report needs its count threshold and grading version. The same ANC on one date can conceal different durations of low counts, and an earlier reassuring count does not dismiss new fever or other infection symptoms. Supportive-care benefit, such as fewer infections, is distinct from cancer control.

evidence.explanation: ANC units, depth, duration, timing and fever definition are retained; equal day-three values do not give equal course or infection probability.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fever with neutropenia is defined by a stated temperature and a stated neutrophil threshold, which a trial or guideline should name. A low count alone does not establish infection, and infection can occur without neutropenia, so the count and the fever are separate findings that together define the syndrome and prompt assessment before any source of infection is found.

points.requirement: Carry the full-extent two-window image meaning: finite plasma DNA outside cells versus an MRI feature within the examined region, without individual cancer-cell counts or a disease census.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The two-window comparison is about scope. A finite plasma aliquot contains extracellular DNA, of which tumour-derived fragments may be one part; breast MRI observes regional, sequence-dependent features rather than individual cancer cells. Contrast enhancement reflects vascular and contrast-delivery behaviour as well as the acquisition protocol; it is not a one-to-one viable-cell count. In the 84-person I-SPY2 MRI pilot, functional tumour volume summed voxels meeting 70% enhancement about two and a half minutes after contrast, inside a manually drawn box around the lesion. A camera-and-stream analogy illustrates those two sampled views without promising that every tumour sheds DNA. Keep the imaging method visible: mammography uses X-rays, ultrasound uses sound, and PET/CT combines tracer-distribution images with anatomical CT images. A formal response category needs its framework, comparison timepoint and findings outside a selected lesion measurement. None of these measurements is an interchangeable all-body tumour-cell number.

review.rationale: Both themes place illustrative oxidation in membrane tails and separate GPX4/glutathione lipid-hydroperoxide reduction from FSP1/CoQ radical-trap regeneration. Generic O icons are not atom counts or assay readings. The image explicitly requires damage, timing, death and rescue and disclaims diagnosis.

points.requirement: Ferroptosis involves iron-dependent membrane-lipid peroxidation causing death. Erastin experiments implicated cystine uptake through system xc-, connecting cysteine and glutathione supply to antioxidant defence. Vulnerable polyunsaturated lipid chains, iron availability and cellular conditions matter; general reactive-oxygen fluorescence does not establish this mechanism.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: GPX4 uses glutathione to reduce lipid hydroperoxides to lipid alcohols. FSP1 provides a parallel coenzyme-Q radical-trapping defence; it does not replace every GPX4 function or describe the whole protection network. Protein abundance alone does not measure protective activity or predict compound sensitivity.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: Assigning ferroptosis needs convergent measurements of death, lipid damage preceding death, iron dependence and appropriately controlled rescue. Independent genetic and chemical perturbations strengthen attribution; rescue alone is not complete proof. Probe chemistry, concentration, nutrients, cell density and observation time can alter results. A lipid-probe ratio and death fraction are different outputs, with no universal diagnostic staining threshold. Live death and rescue tests consume viable model material. Specify lipid-probe oxidation ratios and independently measured death percentages over a stated interval; a marker snapshot does not reconstruct the full causal sequence.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: A culture with abundant GPX4, a general oxidation signal and no death has not demonstrated ferroptosis. Cell-line and xenograft vulnerabilities do not establish tolerable exposure, selective cancer killing or benefit in patients. Alternative defences can confer resistance, so a strong antioxidant programme is not automatically a treatment vulnerability.

points.requirement: Protein abundance reflects synthesis and removal. Pulse labelling or a controlled temporary synthesis block can help estimate turnover but may cause stress. Independent perturbation and restoration help distinguish a selected-substrate effect from a secondary response; enzyme engagement alone does not establish selective killing.

review.auditor: Coordinator integration; not expert sign-off
review.rationale: Both themes separate RNA processing through IRE1/XBP1u-to-XBP1s, PERK phosphorylation of eIF2alpha and ATF6 Golgi traffic/cleavage followed by a nuclear fragment. A phosphate alone does not specify kinase, total message is not splice fraction and branch activity is not death.

points.requirement: ER stress is an imbalance between protein-folding demand and local capacity; the unfolded protein response is an adaptation programme, not the same thing as the stress. IRE1 processes XBP1 RNA, PERK phosphorylates eIF2alpha and ATF6 processing releases a nuclear regulator. Distinct branches can alter folding capacity, incoming translation and disposal.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: ATF6 travels from ER to Golgi for processing; the released fragment, rather than the intact membrane-bound precursor, acts in the nucleus. Total XBP1 RNA differs from its splice-form fraction. Other kinases can phosphorylate eIF2alpha, so one phosphosite cannot identify the whole response.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: Specify preserved material, RNA quality, isoform-specific methods, total-protein controls, timing and identified cell populations. Splice-form fractions, processed ATF6 and defined phosphoprotein signals are different outputs. Increased XBP1 splicing with stable viable-cell counts supports a branch response, not lethal stress; measure growth and death directly and test causality independently. RNA or protein preparations and compatible tissue stains use material; functional dependence tests require viable cells. Report splice-form fractions, defined phosphosite signals or processed fragments with assay-specific controls, rather than a universal UPR-positive treatment threshold.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: XBP1 depletion altered tumour growth and relapse in defined triple-negative breast cancer models, with an HIF1alpha transcriptional interaction. Model findings and patient expression-signature associations do not establish universal XBP1 dependence, an assay cutoff or a treatment benefit. Successful stress adaptation can support survival.

review.auditor: Coordinator integration; not expert sign-off
review.rationale: Both themes locate outer/inner membranes, intermembrane space and matrix; proton pumping is matrix-outward, ATP-synthase return and leak point inward, and electron transfer ends in oxygen-to-water separately. No fixed ratios are claimed. Source review of the foundational reconstitution claim remains open even though the actual image has been viewed.

points.requirement: Distinguish electron transport, proton pumping from the mitochondrial matrix to the intermembrane space, return through ATP synthase and leak. Treat the foundational reconstitution as a named artificial-vesicle coupling experiment, with its own orientation, rather than a universal cellular orientation or fixed proton-to-ATP ratio.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: Respiration and ATP generation are related but different measurements. Mitochondrial and nonmitochondrial oxygen consumption, proton leak and ATP-linked respiration require controlled separation. Respiratory transcripts, normalised oxygen-consumption rates and survival dependence cannot substitute for one another; bulk tissue composition and compensatory fuel use also matter. Oxygen-consumption assays require viable cells or functional preparations rather than routine fixed sections and use or perturb the tested material. Report oxygen per time with justified viable-cell or protein normalisation. Equal baseline respiration and different responses to ATP-synthase inhibition do not by themselves identify which culture will die.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: The fictional oxygen-rate example gives 60 minus 30 = 30 picomoles of oxygen per minute per 10,000 viable cells after ATP-synthase inhibition. This is an inhibitor-sensitive oxygen-rate difference, not picomoles of ATP, a death percentage or a corrected ATP-production calculation. Fuel, normalisation and assay controls remain attached.

evidence.explanation: Exact current field passage, bounded source reading, actual reader body and applicable actual export checks are retained in the batch packet.

points.requirement: Extracellular acidification includes respiratory carbon dioxide as well as glycolytic acid production. Quantitative glycolytic or ATP-rate calculations need appropriate corrections and an identified method version; the contents of the published correction must be checked before adopting a corrected formula or conversion ratio.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Fibroblasts are cells; stroma is a broader compartment that also includes extracellular matrix, vascular structures and other cells. evidence.supportingExcerpt: The limit of blank describes an upper background response at a specified probability. A limit of quantitation requires stated quantitative accuracy, including bias and imprecision goals. The limits answer different questions and have no universal spacing; they may coincide under a particular method and its criteria.

evidence.explanation: Semantic comparison at stated source or fictional-premise scope; hash and containment checks are separate from entailment.
evidence.supportingExcerpt: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. These are questions for matched model, timing and readout; no one control proves specificity or patient benefit, and agreement between similar readouts is not automatically independent mechanistic confirmation.
